editorial:
Imagine waking up to the news that a giant rock is about to hit Earth, and all you have is a massive greenhouse and a bunker your dad left you. That is exactly where you find Ethan, a guy who is already dealing with a lot of sadness and family drama. You will feel the tension build as people around him start to panic and turn on each other. It feels less like a big action movie and more like a personal story about a man trying to keep his head above water while the world literally falls apart around him. The vibe is heavy and lonely, making you wonder if you could handle that kind of pressure.

You will really love the acting here because the lead makes you feel every bit of his pain and fear. The pacing is steady, though some parts in the bunker might feel a bit slow until that radio starts buzzing. One of the best parts is how the movie handles the mystery of who is on the other end of the line. If you want the best experience, you should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the detail in the greenhouse scenes. Or, if you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move for the amazing sound design.
endingExplained: After spending weeks alone, Ethan finally finds the person on the radio. It turns out to be a survivor from a nearby town who reveals that the impact was not as bad as the news said. The twist is that the government hid the fact that many safe zones existed. Ethan leaves his bunker and meets the survivor, showing that hope still exists and that humanity can start over together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves survival stories and character dramas.
